title: The Emergency Years at the Box Office
subtitle: 21 months that reshaped Hindi cinema · Archive Series
summary: Between June 1975 and March 1977, Hindi cinema worked under content regulation that capped action at 90 seconds, banned films mid-release, and saw one film's prints physically burned. Cinema halls stayed full. The multi-starrer became dominant. The Soviet Union was the largest overseas market. Ticket prices, production houses, currency context — the full archive.
